findings.title: Raw publish bearer tokens serialized publicly in GET /api/v1/package response
findings.description: VersionInfo is #[derive(Serialize)] and documented as the GET /api/v1/package/{name} JSON body (storage.rs:56-90). publish() sets author to the raw bearer token when no OAuth session exists (handlers.rs:440-443), persisted in versions.author and loaded back into the response (storage_sqlite.rs:316-330). Any anonymous client can therefore read every static-token publisher's plaintext credential with one curl. The field doc itself states 'The author (publish token)'.
findings.root_cause: T70 quality-signals wiring routed author through the public VersionInfo DTO for server-side badge computation without separating identity (github login) from secret (publish token).
findings.impact: Public unauthenticated credential disclosure: one leaked metadata scrape yields publish rights + org identity for every static-token publisher; tokens are long-lived with no rotation tooling.
findings.recommendation: Add #[serde(skip_serializing)] to VersionInfo.author; store only SHA-256(token) (or github login) in versions.author; rotate existing tokens; add integration test asserting package metadata never contains a seeded token.
findings.fix_guide: 1) Add #[serde(skip_serializing)] to VersionInfo.author (storage.rs:79). 2) In handlers.rs publish (line ~443) and multipart publish (~812), replace .or_else(|| Some(token.to_string())) with sha256-hex of the token (sha2 already a workspace dep). 3) Key is_verified_author on the digest. 4) Migration: UPDATE versions SET author to digest or NULL. 5) Extend tests/registry_tests.rs: seed token, GET package, assert token absent.

effort_estimate.breakdown: DTO flag 5m; digest helper 15m; two handler sites 15m; migration+test 25m

detection_method.query: author.*publish token; VersionInfo Serialize derive; or_else(|| Some(token.to_string()))

references: OWASP API Security API3:2019 Broken Object Property Level Authorization

confidence.rationale: Direct read confirmed Serialize derive on VersionInfo, handler storing raw token as author, and get_package loading that column into the public response

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Code comments explicitly admit the field carries the publish token; no AGENTS.md/convention documents public exposure as a deliberate choice

findings.title: ~/.buff/credentials bearer token written plaintext with no restrictive permissions
findings.description: save_credentials_to serializes the bearer token to TOML and writes it with plain fs::write (registry.rs:236-239); no 0600/ACL hardening. On Unix a default umask yields world-readable 0644. The docstring defers only atomicity ('a future hardening pass can swap in a temp-file + rename'), not permissions. Prior squads flagged this; it remains unhardened.
findings.root_cause: v1.6 milestone simplicity; the credential-store helper was never revisited when registry auth became real (T57 SQLite/OAuth).
findings.impact: Stolen token grants publish rights and registry identity impersonation. Readily exposed on multi-user Unix hosts, via backup jobs, dotfile sync, or any local process reading the user profile.
findings.recommendation: Set 0600 permissions on Unix via std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt after write; document Windows user-profile ACL behavior inline; warn when an existing credentials file is group/world-readable; consider OS keyring long-term.

fix_examples.before:
fs::write(path, text)
    .with_context(|| format!("failed to write credentials to {}", path.display()))?;

findings.fix_guide: 1) After fs::write in save_credentials_to, apply mode 0600 on unix targets (cfg-gated; Windows inherits user-profile ACL â€” add a doc comment). 2) In load_credentials_from, stat the file and bail/warn if unix mode has group/other read bits. 3) Extend tests credentials_round_trip_through_disk to assert the mode on unix. 4) Note in buff-lang-cli/AGENTS.md so the choice is recorded.

confidence.rationale: fs::write with no permission-setting call verified by direct read; Windows path inherits profile ACL, Unix path does not

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Plaintext TOML simplicity IS documented ('kept dead-simple for the v1.6 milestone'), but the docstring defers atomicity only; no convention declares no-permission-hardening deliberate, and a prior squad already flagged it

findings.title: Publish + session tokens stored unhashed (plaintext) in SQLite at rest
findings.description: tokens and sessions tables store raw token strings as PRIMARY KEY (storage_sqlite.rs:88-90, 106-110); add_token INSERTs plaintext (:208-216) and create_session INSERTs the raw UUID session token (:569-576). No hashing anywhere in the crate. WAL mode (init, :194) additionally spreads live copies into registry.db-wal side files.
findings.root_cause: Static-token MVP kept tokens as direct lookup keys; T57 sessions reused the same plaintext-key pattern for OAuth session tokens.
findings.impact: Any read of the DB file, WAL, or a backup (host compromise, leaked backup, debug access) yields every publish credential and live session cookie in cleartext â€” mass account takeover with no further attack step.
findings.recommendation: Store SHA-256 digests as the keys; hash the presented token and compare digests on validate_token/validate_session; migrate existing rows (or force re-login); consider SQLCipher only if threat model demands.

fix_examples.before: INSERT OR IGNORE INTO tokens (token) VALUES (?1)
fix_examples.after:
INSERT OR IGNORE INTO tokens (token_hash) VALUES (?1) -- ?1 = sha256_hex(token)
-- lookup: SELECT 1 FROM tokens WHERE token_hash = ?1 (hash the bearer first)

findings.fix_guide: 1) Rename columns to token_hash / recreate tables (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS won't alter existing DBs â€” add a small ALTER/migration step). 2) Add fn hash_token(&str) -> String using sha2 (workspace dep). 3) Hash in add_token/create_session; hash-before-query in validate_token/validate_session/try_record_publish/delete_session. 4) Buff login client is unaffected (server-side change only). 5) Test: raw token string never appears in the DB file bytes.

effort_estimate.breakdown: hash helper 15m; 6 storage methods 45m; migration 30m; tests 30m

detection_method.query: INSERT INTO tokens / INSERT INTO sessions plaintext

findings.verification_command: Select-String -Path "crates\buff-registry\src\storage_sqlite.rs" -Pattern "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO tokens","INSERT INTO sessions","journal_mode" -Context 2,3

confidence.rationale: Schema and both INSERT sites read directly; grep found no hashing anywhere in buff-registry

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: buff-registry AGENTS.md documents static tokens via add_token and in-memory MVP as deliberate for T126, but says nothing sanctioning plaintext persistence after T57 added durable SQLite + OAuth sessions

findings.title: OAuth sessions never expire - no TTL column or time check
findings.description: sessions schema holds only (token, user_id, created_at) (storage_sqlite.rs:106-110); validate_session (:579-595) performs no time-based check, despite the Storage trait doc promising Ok(None) for 'unknown / expired' (storage.rs:325-331). The buff_session cookie also sets no Max-Age (oauth.rs:290). A leaked cookie is valid indefinitely; logout is the only lifecycle event.
findings.root_cause: T57 session MVP implemented create/validate/delete without a retention policy; the trait contract mentions expiry that was never implemented.
findings.impact: Indefinite identity-token lifetime defeats breach containment; stolen buff_session = permanent GitHub-identity access to publish/org surfaces. Unbounded sessions rows also retain identity linkage forever.
findings.recommendation: Add expires_at column (e.g. created_at + 7 days), enforce in validate_session, periodically DELETE expired rows; document an ALTER TABLE migration for existing databases and a SESSION_TTL env override.

fix_examples.before: SELECT u.github_login, u.github_id FROM sessions s JOIN users u ON s.user_id = u.id WHERE s.token = ?1
fix_examples.after:
DELETE FROM sessions WHERE expires_at < ?2; -- lazy sweep, ?2 = now
SELECT u.github_login, u.github_id FROM sessions s JOIN users u ON s.user_id = u.id WHERE s.token = ?1 AND s.expires_at > ?2

findings.fix_guide: 1) ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN expires_at INTEGER (guard for existing DBs). 2) create_session: insert now + ttl (new SESSION_TTL_ENV, default 604800s). 3) validate_session: add AND expires_at > now + lazy sweep. 4) oauth.rs callback comment update. 5) Test: backdated session validates to None.

effort_estimate.breakdown: migration 20m; two queries 20m; env config 15m; tests 35m

findings.verification_command: Select-String -Path "crates\buff-registry\src\storage_sqlite.rs","crates\buff-registry\src\storage.rs" -Pattern "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions","unknown / expired","SELECT u.github_login" -Context 1,6

confidence.rationale: Zero expir/ttl matches in storage_sqlite.rs; validate_session read in full and contains no time comparison

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: No documentation anywhere claims session expiry is deferred or deliberate; the trait doc actively claims behavior that does not exist

findings.title: No user-data deletion path - users table rows are immutable
findings.description: The route table exposes no DELETE endpoint for accounts or user rows (lib.rs:279-302); only /auth/logout removes a session (oauth.rs:316-334 -> storage_sqlite.rs:597-605). users rows (github_login, github_id, created_at; storage_sqlite.rs:100-105) and versions.author identities persist indefinitely with no erasure or export mechanism, leaving LGPD Art. 16/18 requests technically unfulfillable.
findings.root_cause: Registry MVP scope stopped at publish/download/auth; no data-lifecycle endpoints were planned when identity storage (users/orgs/allowlist) landed in T57.
findings.impact: Data-subject erasure cannot be honored once a real deployment exists; identity linkage (login + id + publish history) retained forever enlarges breach blast radius.
findings.recommendation: Ship authenticated DELETE /auth/account: delete sessions + org_members + users row; NULL/redact versions.author; keep package/version integrity. Link a one-paragraph privacy notice (what is stored, retention, deletion) from the OAuth consent/docs.

fix_examples.after:
.route("/auth/whoami", get(oauth::whoami))
.route("/auth/account", delete(oauth::delete_account)) // deletes sessions + user row, redacts versions.author

findings.fix_guide: 1) Storage trait fn delete_account(github_login) with CASCADE deletes + UPDATE versions SET author = NULL WHERE author = login. 2) Handler requires valid session, deletes, clears cookie. 3) Short privacy notice page (website or docs) linked from the OAuth app description. 4) Integration test: after delete, whoami 401 and user row gone.

effort_estimate.breakdown: trait+sqlite impl 60m; handler+route 30m; notice page 45m; tests 45m

detection_method.query: route( listing; DELETE FROM scan in buff-registry

confidence.rationale: Full route table and all DELETE statements enumerated; no account/user deletion exists

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Registry is pre-deployment MVP (invite-only allowlist, loopback default) and AGENTS.md documents deferred features broadly, so severity stays low; but nothing documents data-subject deletion as intentionally deferred, and the surface collects GitHub identities

Registry itself stores only GitHub login + numeric id (oauth.rs:70-74). No PII collection found - expectation confirmed.

No PII/token logging: buff-registry logs only backend path + bind address via eprintln (main.rs:52,60,66); zero println/tracing/log statements in handlers.rs, oauth.rs, or rate_limit.rs - bearer tokens and usernames are never logged.

IP handling is privacy-clean: per-IP limiter is an in-memory HashMap pruned on every check (rate_limit.rs:44,67), never persisted; the SQLite rate_log table stores token+ts_ms (NOT IP) and is pruned (storage_sqlite.rs:427). X-Forwarded-For spoofability (rate_limit.rs:113) is a rate-limit-bypass security issue, not privacy - out of squad scope.

Website privacy-notice absence judged NOT a top-5 finding: static no-collection site (only Google Fonts third-party requests, website/index.html:11-13); however the OAuth consent flow has no linked privacy notice - folded into AUD-PRIV-005 recommendation.
buff_oauth_state CSRF cookie lacks the Secure flag (oauth.rs:199) unlike buff_session (oauth.rs:290) - negligible: state also travels in the URL, TTL 300s, double-submit validation.
buff-jupyter connection files contain HMAC key material but follow the standard Jupyter kernel protocol contract (ipykernel parity), local-file surface only - no finding.
Download counts are aggregate-only (downloads table: name/version/count, storage_sqlite.rs:124-129,691-701) - no per-IP or per-user download tracking exists, confirming prior squads.
